newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK government welcomes choice of China's envoy.
newsitem.headline: HK government welcomes choice of China's envoy.

text.p: The Hong Kong government welcomed Beijing's announcement on Thursday that veteran diplomat Ma Yuzhen would be the mainland's top civilian official in the territory after the handover to China on July 1.
"The community will be glad that the appointment of Mr Ma Yuzhen has been announced," the government said in a statement.

As head of the Chinese Foreign Ministry Office in Hong Kong, Ma will be responsible for foreign affairs matters in the territory, which will become a Special Administrative Region of China at midnight on June 30 after 156 years of British rule.
"Hong Kong people will no doubt be interested to hear more details of the establishment of this new office, including the size of its staff and its functions," the statement said.
Hong Kong will run its own domestic affairs after the handover, but foreign affairs and defence will remain under the auspices of the central government in Beijing.
Democratic Party vice-chairman Yeung Sum said Ma's diplomatic experience in London and his understanding of the handover issues made him an appropriate person for the job.
"As a representative of the Chinese Foreign Ministry, he should truly reflect the concerns and worries of Hong Kong people to the Chinese central government," Yeung said.
A civil service veteran of more than 40 years, Ma now holds the post of vice-minister of the information office of the State Council, or cabinet.

Ma, 62, has been ambassador to Britain and has held senior diplomatic posts at missions in Ghana and Burma. He was deputy division chief of the Foreign Ministry's information department for more than a decade.
